opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Erika Bolton (E002) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin access to Payroll. Admin is only permitted if the employee's role owns the system; Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. As an Analyst, the maximum permitted access is write, so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB check: Erika Bolton (E002) is a contractor with basic security training (note says full-time, but Security DB shows contractor). Contractors with basic training may have at most read access for Payroll; write requires advanced training and admin is never permitted. Requested admin, so grant the maximum permitted: read.
reason: Erika Bolton (E002) requested admin access to Payroll. Admin is never permitted for either classification: admin requires the role to own the system (only Payroll Specialist owns Payroll, and Erika is an Analyst), and contractors can never have admin. Per the Security DB check, Erika is a contractor with basic security training, so the maximum permitted access is read (write requires advanced training). Since the requested level (admin) is above the maximum, grant the maximum: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Erika Bolton (E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Two notes from HR and Security:
- Note 1 (HR): role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation: write. Says admin only if role owns system; Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist; Analyst max is write.
- Note 2 (Security): role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation: read. Security DB shows contractor with basic training; contractors with basic training at most read.

Conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. As Approver, I need to make a decision. The notes stay in memory. Security DB check seems authoritative on employment type? The policy: full-time employees up to write, admin only if role owns system. Contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Either way, admin is not permitted. The requested level is admin, which is above the maximum in both cases. So grant the maximum.

But which maximum? If full-time Analyst: max write. If contractor with basic training: max read.

The Security note indicates the employee is a contractor per Security DB. Security data presumably is more authoritative for access decisions. So max = read.

Requested admin, above max, so grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.
